rationale: D13: a friend function DEFINED inside a class body is NOT a member of that class, so its body's reads must not be attributed to the class. CP2 (cpp review) established that a friend declaration mints no member symbol — `friend void helper();` declares someone else's function and the inner declaration node previously minted a (private) Method for it. That rule is right for a DECLARATION and was too broad for a DEFINITION, which has a BODY whose reads belong to the friend and not to the class. MEASURED on absl/random/uniform_int_distribution.h:81-87, where `param_type` has member functions named `a()` and `b()` AND an in-class friend `operator==` whose parameters are also named `a` and `b`: the analyzer published `uses param_type -> b`, the enclosing CLASS as the owner of a read of a PARAMETER. That is wrong twice over — the read belongs to the friend rather than the class, and the class has members of the same name, so the edge cannot be told apart from reading those members. It surfaced as the single UNEXPLAINED analyzer edge on abseil-cpp (1 of 19,362), one of three unexplained rows across 1,028 files, all one class. The fix keeps CP2 exactly as it was for a declaration (still no symbol) and only re-OWNs a definition's body, so that the class is never the owner. Two details the first attempt got wrong and measuring caught, both recorded in the analyzer: (1) the enclosing-scope helper initially returned the CONTAINING CLASS, which is the one scope a friend's body can never belong to, so it re-attributed the reads to exactly the owner the fix was written to remove and the reproducer did not move; (2) an unnamed enclosing scope fell back to the string "anonymous", which is the analyzer's own no-name SENTINEL — D7's contract calls that collision out explicitly — and it moved 239 edges ONTO the sentinel corpus-wide, trading one wrong named owner for a worse one. Both are why `anonymous` appears in forbidRelationships here: the fix must not launder a wrong owner into the sentinel. The `OutOfLine` block is the CONTROL and the reason this pin is not one-sided — an out-of-line member definition's body is already owned correctly, so a fix that simply pushed every function body to `global` would fail here. The `forbidRelationships` rows are scoped to `type: uses` deliberately: `contains param_type -> a` and `-> b` are CORRECT edges (the class does contain those members), and an unscoped forbid on the same (from,to) pair fails the fixture on the legitimate edge. The first version of this file did exactly that and was caught by the runner — which is the failure mode `matchConstraints` is designed to expose. ---- THE 2026-10-21 REVISION, AND WHY IT IS NOT A RE-BASELINE ---- This file was authored on 2026-10-01 (commit 1d214319a, "D13 gates 94") against the analyzer of that day, which re-owned a friend definition's body to the FILE scope and minted NO symbol for the friend at all. The analyzer's friend handling changed LATER, on measured evidence, in commit 3724013a3 (2026-10-13, "SIX ANALYZERS TAKEN FROM MAIN ON MEASURED EVIDENCE, ONE KEPT"), and that is the change the companion fixture `cpp/friend-definition-published` (CP3) pins: a friend definition is a FREE FUNCTION in the enclosing namespace (C++ [class.friend]; found through ADL, which is how nlohmann's `to_json`/`from_json`/`operator==` serializers are picked up), so it is PUBLISHED as a `Function` owned by the scope that encloses the class, never by the class. The reason was measured and is recorded in the analyzer: publishing nothing for those free functions was the corpus's largest real loss — every edge naming one (`operator==`, `to_json`, `from_json`, `int_to_string`) was unresolvable. So from 2026-10-13 the friend definition HAS a symbol, and its own body's reads are owned by that symbol; the FILE scope no longer owns them. This file was never re-read when that landed, so it went RED, and the Lead's ruling L-2026-10-21 (validation/m14/verification/LEAD-RULINGS-2026-10-21.md, id L-2026-10-21-02) had to settle which of the two AUTHORED CONTRACTS governs. The ruling's own clauses are what this revision pins, one for one: (1) "A friend, declaration OR definition, never mints a member symbol of the class" — the symbol may exist, but the CLASS's member key space must not hold it, so the forbid is now SCOPED to the class-owned form (`ownerName: param_type`), the class-contains-the-friend edge is forbidden, and the class-owned spelling is pinned absent BY COUNT; (2) "An operator spelling is not in the published key space of the class's members", with the lane's own measurement as the reason (the class has real members `a` and `b` AND an in-class friend `operator==` whose PARAMETERS are also named `a` and `b`, so publishing the operator as a class member would make `uses param_type -> b` undecidable) — which is why the friend's PARAMETER reads are now pinned in the NEGATIVE direction (`uses operator== -> a` and `-> b` must NOT exist: a parameter is a local, and publishing it as a use of a symbol named `a` would re-create exactly the undecidability the ruling names); (3) "the definition's body is owned by the lexically enclosing scope, never by the class" — the friend free function IS a symbol in the lexically enclosing scope, so owning its own body's reads is that clause satisfied, and the class is not the owner, which is the clause the forbids below pin. WHAT THIS REVISION KEEPS: every live prohibition of the original — the class never owns the friend's reads, the `anonymous` sentinel never owns them, a friend DECLARATION mints no symbol (`helper`), and the out-of-line member body keeps its own owner. WHAT IT ADDS, so the change earns its keep rather than moving the goalposts: the class-owned operator spelling is pinned BY COUNT and by the scoped forbid; the class-contains-the-friend edge is forbidden; the friend's parameter reads are pinned absent; and the friend symbol's count is pinned at exactly 1 (the dedupe claim: one definition, one symbol). The measured pre-fix baseline is recorded in validation/m14/verification/CPP-CELL-2026-10-21.md: the fixture suite reads 55 pass / 1 fail on the PRE-FIX analyzer tree (sha256 f5962cc60ce5f04f5f2c7481b57f253a8488d77be28f582f7429c0502c6a3d25, the tree at 81cc4aea9^) AND 55 pass / 1 fail after this lane's receiver-wave commit — the same single failure either way, so the receiver-wave change moved no fixture result, and "pre-existing" is a number with a root rather than a claim.
